question: The situation in the Ethiopian region of Tigray has deteriorated once again in recent months. Despite earlier commitments, access to humanitarian aid remains restricted. Furthermore, drone attacks have been reported again in recent weeks. Caritas Ethiopia is one of the few organisations still providing aid to the estimated one million internally displaced people in Tigray.

According to the Catholic Bishop of Adigrat, on 20 September a Caritas Ethiopia lorry, which was en route to the Sheraro refugee camp with food aid, was destroyed by a drone strike carried out by the Ethiopian government forces. 1.
What has the Commission’s response been to the incident on 20 September, in which a food convoy operated by Caritas Ethiopia was attacked by a government drone?
What steps will the Commission take to remind the Ethiopian Government of its obligations under international humanitarian law and to prevent future attacks on humanitarian aid convoys in Tigray?

During the war from 2020 to 2022, the EU suspended budget support to the Ethiopian Government due to the blockade of humanitarian aid and human rights violations in Tigray. Does the Commission consider the resumption of EU budget support to Ethiopia to be justified as long as the Ethiopian Government fails to fulfil its obligations regarding humanitarian aid and humanitarian food convoys in Tigray continue to be targeted by drone attacks?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) The EU is extremely concerned by the continued escalation of violence in Ethiopia and its impact on civilians, including humanitarian workers. The EU strongly condemned strikes affecting humanitarian convoys and any instance of denial of humanitarian access.

Respect for international humanitarian law (IHL) and the protection of civilians, including humanitarian personnel and assets, are non-negotiable. The EU consistently recalls these obligations in its public messaging1, including in the latest statement from the High Representative/Vice-President on behalf of the EU of 5 October 2026, and in its bilateral contacts with the parties to the conflict.

All EU diplomatic engagements for de-escalation are accompanied by strong humanitarian diplomacy efforts on the need for all parties to comply with IHL and guarantee safe, unimpeded, and uninterrupted humanitarian access so that assistance can reach those in need.

The resumption of EU budget support was part of a broader effort to engage constructively with Ethiopia, to create a favourable environment for dialogue, including on issues such as IHL and human rights law. This engagement remains subject to continued assessment.

The EU will continue to encourage the resumption of talks and to support the African Unionled mediation efforts, while reiterating the importance of accountability, protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian law and human rights laws.
1 Commissioner Hadja Lahbib, X post, 28 September 2026,
